question: Within the 667 first-flux sectors reached by <=2 physical red-X edges, do equal sector priors predict the canonical base error's complete all-zero-charge first-record likelihood, and can a first-law base census fit the inherited projector budget?

hypotheses.prior_insufficient: At least one exact-prior-equivalent sector group has distinct canonical-base first-record likelihoods, directly rejecting prior equivalence as a public-law shortcut.
hypotheses.necessary_not_sufficient: Canonical-base likelihoods coincide within each exact-prior group, a necessary witness only; full operator-law symmetry remains unproved because other records and private errors were not evaluated.
hypotheses.cost_censored: Projected direct first-projector work for all 667 base records exceeds 65,536 terms or CPU exceeds 60 seconds; stop before any Born evaluation and preserve cost finding.

frozen_model: R6AF ideal periodic L=2 D4 orbit, 36 IID red-X physical edges at p_X=1/10 and p_Z=0. J6O signal-only pre-action complete 24-bit first observation uses each sector's public flux, all-zero charge and vacuum=1-charge. The unique J8P minimum-weight <=2-edge representative is private generation/scoring provenance, never a public action input. Both fixed relation-free public charge actions and their action-conditioned full-binary second records remain unchanged but are not evaluated. No noisy history, score, schedule comparison or threshold.

branches: For all 667 J8P reached sectors, preflight every canonical minimum-weight representative's eligible first-star means, pairwise commutation, deterministic conflicts, variable projector count and combined 2^v exact first-law term cost. If joint cost fits, evaluate its specified complete all-zero-charge first likelihood and exact prior-weighted base joint mass.

Within each J8P minimum-support/flux-weight/exact-prior class, count distinct canonical-base first likelihoods. Form only a conservative omitted-error posterior upper bound U/(A+U) with U equal to the full sector prior minus base prior and A equal to exact base joint mass; never call it evaluated omitted likelihood or full-channel information.
matrix.independent_unit: One distinct reached first-flux sector with its prospectively fixed J8P canonical minimum-weight private base error. Exact rational laws; no stochastic uncertainty.
matrix.integrity: Pin all inputs and runner, replay 667 distinct J8P rows and J8O vacuum/edge-0 base likelihoods, verify eligible sites match public flux, pairwise first-star commutation, deterministic-site reduction, exact likelihood in [0,1], disjoint prior partition, 65,536-term preflight before any Born evaluation, CPU/hash stability, and zero second-law/stochastic work. Equal prior or equal base likelihood is not an operator-law symmetry proof.

acceptance: Joint projected exact first-law cost within inherited ceiling before any Born call, or a recorded fail-closed censoring
Exact 667 canonical-base complete first-record likelihoods and prior-weighted base masses when feasible, with J8O replay
Count of distinct base likelihoods in each equal-prior class and conservative omitted-error posterior upper bounds, with no full-channel inference
stop_rule: Stop after the 667 frozen base records or first integrity, 65,536-term, or 60-CPU-second violation. Never add a third observation, extra error/flux sector, alternative first charge record, omitted complete law, second law, schedule arm, bootstrap, or threshold fit. A loose bound or equal-likelihood class remains a limited result.
